recipes.name: Classic Hummus
recipes.flavorProfile: Smooth, nutty and bright with lemon, with a soft garlic edge and a little warmth from cumin.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chickpeas bring plant protein and fiber, and tahini adds calcium, iron and mostly unsaturated fat, so a few spoonfuls make a filling spread or dip.

ingredients.cutPrep: cooked or canned, drained and rinsed
ingredients.prepNote: 1½ cans (15 oz), drained, or about 1 cup dried, cooked
about 3 tbsp juice, from 1 to 2 lemons

instructions: Stir the lemon juice and cold water together in a small cup. Whisk the tahini with the olive oil in a second cup.
Put the chickpeas, garlic, salt, cumin and cayenne in a food processor and process for about 15 seconds, until almost fully ground.
Scrape down the bowl. With the machine running, pour in the lemon and water in a steady stream, then process for about 1 minute.
Scrape down again. With the machine running, pour in the tahini and oil in a steady stream and process for about 15 seconds, until the hummus is smooth and creamy.
Move it to a bowl, cover and let it stand at room temperature for about 30 minutes so the flavors blend, then serve.
Keep it covered in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. Stir before using, and loosen with a spoonful of water if it has thickened.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the chickpeas.
From the chickpeas and the tahini together.
Mostly from the tahini.

recipes.curationNote: America's Test Kitchen, Classic Hummus for every amount and step: one 15 oz can makes about 2 cups. Ours is 12 servings of 1/4 cup, about 3 cups, so every amount is 1½ times the source.

recipes.name: Homemade Vegetable Stock
recipes.flavorProfile: Light, clean and savory, sweet from onion and carrot, with herb notes from parsley, thyme and bay.
recipes.healthBenefit: A stock made from vegetables and water with no salt added lets each soup be seasoned to taste, and carries far less sodium than a bouillon powder or cube.

ingredients.prepNote: a little under half a head

instructions: Heat the oil in a very large pot over medium-high heat. Add the carrot, onion, fennel, celery root, garlic, parsley, bay leaves, rosemary and thyme and cook for about 15 minutes, until golden and starting to soften.
Add the water and bring to a boil. Add the peppercorns, lower the heat, cover and simmer for 2 hours.
Strain, pressing on the vegetables, and throw the solids away. Cool, then refrigerate covered for up to 5 days, or freeze in 1 cup portions.
It has no salt, so season the dish the stock goes into.

nutritionHighlights.note: Very little, since no salt or bouillon goes in.
Some passes into the water from the vegetables as it simmers.

recipes.curationNote: Sur La Table, Vegetable stock for every amount and step (3 tbsp olive oil, 3 carrots, 2 onions, 1 fennel bulb, 1 celery root, ½ head garlic, parsley, bay, rosemary, thyme and peppercorns in 16 cups water), scaled to 3 litres of water. Unsalted, as the source is. The strained vegetables are counted in full, the same as the oat milk counts all its oats, so the nutrient totals overstate what reaches the bowl.

recipes.name: Homemade Chicken Stock
recipes.flavorProfile: Rich, savory and rounded, with body from the bones and a soft note of onion, garlic and bay.
recipes.healthBenefit: A stock simmered from chicken bones with no salt added gives soups depth and some gelatin, with far less sodium than a stock cube.

ingredients.prepNote: about 3 lb chicken backs, necks and wings, or a roast chicken carcass, hacked into 2 inch pieces and simmered in 2880 ml (12 cups) cold water; counted as 2880 g unsalted chicken bone stock (1 g per ml), since the bones are not eaten

instructions: Put the chicken pieces and cold water in a large stockpot and bring them to a boil over medium high heat, 15 to 20 minutes.
Skim off the foam that rises. Add the onion, garlic and bay leaves, then turn the heat down so it barely simmers, around 190 to 200°F (88 to 93°C).
Simmer partly covered for 2 to 4 hours, skimming now and then. Longer gives more body.
Strain through a fine sieve and discard the bones and vegetables. You should have about 3 quarts (12 cups).
Cool it quickly, refrigerate overnight, and lift off the fat that sets on top.
Keep it in the refrigerator for 1 to 2 days or freeze in 1 cup portions for 3 to 4 months. Salt the dish it goes into, not the stock.

nutritionHighlights.note: Very little, since no salt or stock cube goes in.
A small amount, mostly gelatin drawn from the bones.

citations.source: America's Test Kitchen, All-Purpose Chicken Stock
Center for Science in the Public Interest, Easy Homemade Chicken Stock

recipes.curationNote: ATK proportions (3 lb bones, 12 cups water, 1 onion, 3 garlic, 3 bay, about 3 quarts made, keeps 2 days chilled or 4 months frozen), with the longer 3 to 4 hour simmer CSPI uses for a carcass offered as a range. The bones and water are counted as the Japanese food table row for unsalted chicken bone stock (torigara), 1 g per ml of water, since no row holds bones and counting Meat Chicken would claim the meat itself is eaten. The onion and garlic are counted on top under the strained-solids convention, so the totals run a little high. Replaces the stock cube plus water rows in the chicken vegetable soup.

recipes.name: Yellow Mustard
recipes.flavorProfile: Mild, tangy and bright yellow, with a soft heat that mellows after a day in the jar.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mustard seed and turmeric bring a little selenium and the spice compounds that give it color, and a spoonful carries almost no fat or sugar.

ingredients.cutPrep: minced and mashed to a paste with the salt

instructions: Whisk the water, mustard, salt, turmeric, garlic paste and paprika in a small saucepan until smooth.
Cook over low heat, stirring often, for 35 to 40 minutes, until it is a thick paste. Keep the kitchen well aired.
Stir in the vinegar and cook 7 to 10 minutes more. It thickens as it cools.
Cool, then keep in a covered jar in the refrigerator for up to 3 months. It is very sharp at first and mellows with time. Thin with a little cool water if it gets too thick.

nutritionHighlights.note: Mustard seed is one of the richer plant sources of selenium for its weight.
About 190 mg per tablespoon from the salt.

recipes.name: Almond Milk
recipes.flavorProfile: Light, nutty and faintly sweet, thinner than cow's milk.
recipes.healthBenefit: Made at home it is almonds and water only, so it brings vitamin E and a little calcium with no added sugar or gums.
instructions: Soak the almonds overnight in plenty of water, then drain and rinse them and pour that water away.
Blend the almonds with the 1200 ml fresh water and the salt on high for about 2 minutes, until creamy.
Strain through a nut-milk bag or a cloth-lined sieve, squeezing well. Keep in the fridge and shake before use; it keeps 3 to 4 days.

nutritionHighlights.note: Almonds are one of the richest food sources of vitamin E.
Lower than dairy milk unless fortified, so it does not replace dairy calcium.

citations.source: Minimalist Baker, How to Make Almond Milk

recipes.curationNote: The strained almond pulp is still counted in the nutrients, since the database has no figure for what passes the cloth.

recipes.name: Curry Powder
recipes.flavorProfile: Warm, earthy and gently hot, led by coriander, cumin and turmeric, with sweet notes from cinnamon and cardamom.
recipes.healthBenefit: A blend of single spices with no salt or fillers, so it seasons without adding sodium.
instructions: Measure the turmeric, coriander, cumin, cinnamon, ginger, mustard, white pepper if using, fenugreek, cardamom, cloves, nutmeg, cayenne and black pepper into a bowl, and stir them together well.
Keep in a closed jar away from light and use within 3 months.

nutritionHighlights.note: Cumin and turmeric add a little iron per spoonful.
None added.

citations.source: Whole New Mom, Mild curry powder

recipes.name: Seitan
recipes.flavorProfile: Savory and chewy, with a meaty bite that takes on the broth it simmers in.
recipes.healthBenefit: Very high in protein for its calories. It is wheat gluten, so it is off the table for celiac disease and gluten sensitivity.

components.note: the seitan takes up about 1 cup of the 6 cups it simmers in; the rest is kept as broth

ingredients.prepNote: the share of 2 tablespoons in the broth that the seitan takes up

instructions: Mix the gluten, chickpea flour, nutritional yeast, salt, garlic powder and smoked paprika with the water until a ball forms. Knead on a clean surface for about 5 minutes until elastic.
Shape it into a log and let it rest for 5 minutes.

Bring the stock, 2 tablespoons of cider vinegar and 1 teaspoon of liquid smoke to a simmer in a pot just big enough to keep the log fully under the liquid. Lower it in, partly cover, and simmer for 1 hour.
Lift it out and let it cool until you can handle it, then slice, crumble or cut it as you need. Keep the broth for soup.

nutritionHighlights.note: About 30 g per 150 g serving.
Made from wheat gluten, so it is not for celiac disease.

citations.source: Live Eat Learn, How to make seitan

recipes.name: Tomato Ketchup
recipes.flavorProfile: Thick, sweet and sharp, with warm spice from allspice, clove and cinnamon.
recipes.healthBenefit: Cooking tomatoes down concentrates lycopene, and made at home the sugar and salt are what you choose. It still carries sugar, so it is a condiment, not a vegetable.

ingredients.prepNote: whole, in a spice bag, taken out
about 1½ sticks, crushed, in a spice bag, taken out
whole, about 2 tsp, in a spice bag, taken out
about 1½ Tbsp, in a spice bag, taken out

instructions: Dip the tomatoes in boiling water until the skins split, then into cold water. Peel, core and quarter them.
Put the tomatoes, onion and cayenne in a large pot and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes. Cover, turn off the heat and let stand 20 minutes.
Tie the cloves, cinnamon, allspice and celery seed in a spice bag and bring it to a boil in the vinegar. Take the bag out.
Add the vinegar to the tomatoes and boil for about 30 minutes, then press through a food mill or sieve and return to the pot.
Add the sugar and salt and simmer gently, stirring often, until it has cooked down by half or holds its shape on a spoon.
Keep in the refrigerator, or fill hot pint jars leaving ⅛ inch of headspace and process in a boiling-water canner for 15 minutes (20 minutes above 1,000 ft, 25 above 6,000 ft).

nutritionHighlights.note: Cooked tomato gives up more lycopene than raw.
About 2.5 g added sugar per tablespoon.
About 75 mg per tablespoon.

citations.source: National Center for Home Food Preservation: Tomato ketchup

recipes.curationNote: The skins and seeds pressed out in step 1 are still counted, since the database has no figure for strained tomato.

recipes.name: Sambal Oelek
recipes.flavorProfile: Fiery, fresh and salty, with the bright taste of raw red chili.
recipes.healthBenefit: Raw chili keeps its vitamin C, and a spoonful flavors a whole dish.
instructions: Pulse the chilies with the water in a food processor to a coarse paste.
Heat the paste in a saucepan over medium heat for 3 to 5 minutes.
Stir in the vinegar and salt and keep cooking for about 10 minutes, stirring often.
Let it cool to room temperature. It can be used right away, and tastes best after a night in the refrigerator. Keep it refrigerated.

nutritionHighlights.note: Raw red chili is rich in vitamin C.
About 115 mg per tablespoon.
